clips.caption:
Kevin Trudeau's guest on the show is a hormone-replacement coach who says he won't touch soy and won't put a client on it.

Most soy grown in America is genetically modified and gets added into food as a cheap filler, often without most people realizing it's there.

His concern: soy can raise estrogen, and that can lower testosterone, add water retention, raise blood pressure and bring on brain fog.

Kevin Trudeau's takeaway: check the ingredient list, not just the nutrition label, since soy hides in packaged food that never mentions it on the front.

What's actually hiding in your pantry?

#kevintrudeau #soy #hormonehealth #healthtruth #readthelabel #wellness

Kevin Trudeau's guest explains a question most people never ask their doctor: not "is my number in range," but "what's the trend."

Ranges for blood tests have shifted over the decades, and they differ by country, so "in range" alone tells you very little.

What matters more: has that number been tested over years, and is it moving up, down, or staying put. A single blood panel is a snapshot; a trend is the real story.

Next time you get blood work done, ask to see last year's numbers next to this year's.

#kevintrudeau #bloodwork #healthtruth #knowyourbody #askquestions #wellness

Kevin Trudeau's guest, who has formulated testosterone boosters for the supplement industry since 2011, is blunt about how well most of them actually work.

His estimate: a big share of the effect from herbs like tongkat ali and maca is placebo, and the real boost in testosterone numbers is small.

What does work, in his telling, is the marketing. Big budgets make a bottle feel like it is "juicing up your testosterone" the first time you take it.

Kevin Trudeau's question for the viewer: before buying a booster, would you still believe in it without the label?

#kevintrudeau #testosterone #supplements #healthtruth #readthelabel #wellness

Kevin Trudeau's guest clears up a word that scares a lot of people for no reason: peptide.

When he first learned about them in 2011, peptides were lumped in with performance-enhancing drugs in the headlines. In reality, he says, they are nothing more than short chains of amino acids, the same building blocks already found naturally in protein.

Some are taken from outside the body, but the chain itself is not some foreign chemical; it is the same material your body already uses to build itself.

Does knowing that change how you'd read a supplement label?

#kevintrudeau #peptides #supplements #healthtruth #aminoacids #wellness
